info.title: Flashduty Open API
info.description: Public HTTP API for the Flashduty incident management platform — incidents, notification templates, channels, schedules, monitors, RUM, and platform administration. Every operation is authenticated with an `app_key` query parameter issued from the Flashduty console under Account → APP Keys. Responses follow a uniform envelope: `{ request_id, data }` on success, `{ request_id, error }` on failure.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **300 requests/minute**; **100 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- Use `POST /rum/field/list` to discover available field keys for each scope.
- The `scope` must be one of: `session`, `view`, `action`, `error`, `resource`, `long_task`, `vital`, `issue`, `sourcemap`.
- Pass `dql` to further filter events before counting. DQL syntax follows the RUM query language.
- Pass `sql` with a WHERE-clause only (no SELECT) for SQL-style filtering.
- Default limit is 100; maximum is 100.
- Time range is required (`start_time` / `end_time` in Unix epoch **milliseconds**). Maximum span is 31 days.

## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- `type` defaults to `browser` when omitted for backward compatibility.
- Set `near` from 1 to 20 to include source-code snippets around converted frames.
- For Android NDK native crashes, provide `arch` and `source_type: ndk` so the backend routes to native symbolication.
- For iOS crash stacks, pass `binary_images` so addresses can be relocated against the uploaded dSYM files.
- `no_cache` is intended for debugging and bypasses cached enrich results.

post.description: Run one or more SQL-style RUM data queries over a bounded time range.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- Send 1 to 10 queries in one request; each query `id` becomes a key in the response object.
- `start_time` and `end_time` are required Unix epoch milliseconds. The maximum time range is 31 days.
- Use `format: table` for tabular results, or `format: time_series` for bucketed time-series results.
- For `time_series`, `interval` defaults to 3600 seconds and `max_points` defaults to 1226 when omitted.
- `search_after_ctx` is returned by paginated table queries and can be sent back to continue scanning.

post.description: Return the application, device, session bounds, and views recorded for a replayable session.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- Returns `InvalidParameter` if the session does not exist, or if it has no replay data recorded (`session_has_replay` is false).
- Returns `InvalidParameter` if no views are found within the session's time window.
- Pass `ts` to disambiguate when a `session_id` has been reused across different time windows.

post.description: Page through the recorded replay segments of a session, as presigned URLs or a raw stream.

x-mint.content:
## Restrictions

| Aspect | Value |
| ------ | ----- |
| Rate limits | **1,000 requests/minute**; **50 requests/second** per account |
| Permissions | None — any valid `app_key` can call this operation |

## Usage

- When `url_mode` is `false` (default), the response streams `application/x-ndjson` — one decompressed replay segment JSON object per line — and is **not** wrapped in the standard envelope. The pagination cursor for the next call is returned in the `X-Search-After-Ctx` response header instead of a body field.
- When `url_mode` is `true`, the response is a normal JSON envelope containing presigned download URLs (valid 1 hour) instead of the raw segment bytes.
- Pass `ts` to seek to the most recent full-snapshot segment at or before that time, instead of paging from the start of the session.
- `limit` accepts 1-99; values of 100 or more are rejected.

200.description: Success. Shape depends on `url_mode` — see Usage.

X-Search-After-Ctx.description: Base64-encoded pagination cursor for the next call. Only set in streaming mode (`url_mode: false`).

schema.description: Newline-delimited JSON (NDJSON). Each line is one decompressed replay segment record (rrweb-format events), streamed directly and not wrapped in the standard envelope.

AppKeyAuth.name: app_key
AppKeyAuth.description: App key issued from the Flashduty console under Account → APP Keys. Required on every public API call. Keep it secret — it grants the same access as the owning account.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request — usually a missing or malformed parameter.

error.message: The specified parameter is not valid.

Forbidden.description: The app_key is valid but lacks permission for this operation.

NotFound.description: The referenced resource does not exist or has been deleted. Note: Flashduty historically returns HTTP 400 with code `ResourceNotFound` for missing domain entities; a true 404 is reserved for unknown routes.

error.message: The resource you request is not found

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limit hit. Either the global API limit, a per-account limit, or a per-integration limit.

ServerError.description: Unexpected server-side error. Include the request_id when reporting.

error.message: We encountered an internal error, and it has been reported. Please try again later.

DutyError.description: Error payload inside the response envelope. Present only on non-2xx responses.

message.description: Human-readable error message, localized by the caller's Accept-Language. May contain field names, IDs, or other context from the failing request.
message.example: The specified parameter template_id is not valid.

EmptyObject.description: An empty object. Returned as the `data` payload by operations whose success signal is simply the absence of an error.

EmptyResponse.description: Empty response body. The server returns `data: null` on success.

ErrorCode.description:
Flashduty error code enum. Every failed API response sets `error.code` to one of these stable wire strings. HTTP status is informational — the authoritative signal is the enum value.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `OK` | 200 | Reserved — not returned on real errors. |
| `InvalidParameter` | 400 | A required parameter is missing or failed validation. |
| `BadRequest` | 400 | Generic 400 used when no more specific code fits. |
| `InvalidContentType` | 400 | The `Content-Type` header is not `application/json`. |
| `ResourceNotFound` | 400 | The referenced resource does not exist. Note: returned as HTTP 400, not 404 (historical choice). |
| `NoLicense` | 400 | The feature is license-gated and no active license was found. |
| `ReferenceExist` | 400 | Deletion blocked — other entities still reference this resource. |
| `Unauthorized` | 401 | `app_key` is missing, invalid, or expired. |
| `BalanceNotEnough` | 402 | Billing-gated operation with insufficient account balance. |
| `AccessDenied` | 403 | Authenticated but lacking the permission required for this operation. |
| `RouteNotFound` | 404 | The request URL path is not a known route. |
| `MethodNotAllowed` | 405 | The HTTP method is not allowed on this otherwise-known path. |
| `UndonedOrderExist` | 409 | An outstanding billing order blocks this new one. Wait and retry. |
| `RequestLocked` | 423 | Operation temporarily locked due to repeated failures. |
| `EntityTooLarge` | 413 | Request body exceeds the configured max size. |
| `RequestTooFrequently` | 429 | Rate limit hit — API-global, per-account, or per-integration. |
| `RequestVerifyRequired` | 428 | Second-factor verification required but not supplied. |
| `DangerousOperation` | 428 | High-risk operation requires MFA verification. |
| `InternalError` | 500 | Unhandled server-side error. Include `request_id` in the bug report. |
| `ServiceUnavailable` | 503 | A backend dependency is unavailable. Try again later. |

id.description: Client-supplied query ID. The same value is used as the key in the response object.

dql.description: Optional RUM DQL filter expression used together with SQL validation.

format.description: Output format. `table` returns rows; `time_series` returns bucketed time-series rows.

interval.description: Time bucket interval in seconds for `time_series` queries.

max_points.description: Maximum number of points for `time_series` queries.

time_zone.description: IANA time zone name used when evaluating time functions, such as `Asia/Shanghai`.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque cursor returned by a previous table query for continuing pagination.

disable_sampling.description: When true, asks the query engine to avoid sampling when possible.

RumDataQueryOutput.description: Result for one query. Failed subqueries populate `error`; successful ones populate `data`.

RumDataQueryRequest.description: Batch of RUM data queries over a bounded time range.

start_time.description: Start of the query window, Unix epoch milliseconds.

end_time.description: End of the query window, Unix epoch milliseconds. Maximum 31-day span.

queries.description: Queries to execute concurrently. 1 to 10 queries are allowed.

RumDataQueryResponse.description: Map from request query ID to that query's result or error.

RumDataQueryResult.description: Rows and metadata returned by one RUM data query.

search_after_ctx.description: Opaque cursor for continuing paginated table queries.

fields.description: Column metadata for the values matrix.

values.description: Rows returned by the query. Each row aligns with `fields` by index.

interval.description: Effective time bucket interval in seconds for time-series queries.

RumDataSamplingDecision.description: Sampling metadata when the query engine uses sampled data.

scale_factor.description: Multiplier used to scale sampled counts back to estimated full counts.

selected_tablets.description: Storage tablets selected for the sampled query.

RumFacetCountRequest.description: Parameters for counting facet value distribution.

facet_key.description: The field key to count value distribution for.

facet_value.description: When set, filter events where `facet_key` equals this value before counting. Accepts string, number, or boolean.

start_time.description: Start of the time range, Unix epoch milliseconds.

end_time.description: End of the time range, Unix epoch milliseconds. Maximum 31-day span.

dql.description: RUM DQL filter expression applied before counting.

sql.description: SQL WHERE clause (no SELECT) for additional filtering.

limit.description: Maximum number of top values to return. Default 100, maximum 100.

RumFacetCountResponse.description: Top N facet values sorted by count descending.

description.description: Description of what this field captures.

value_type.description: Data type of the field value.

show_type.description: Display type in the analytics UI.

unit_family.description: Measurement unit family, e.g. `time`, `bytes`. Empty for dimensionless fields.

edit_able.description: True if this is a custom field that can be edited by the user.

is_facet.description: True if value distribution counting is supported for this field.

enum_values.description: Predefined enumerable values for this field. Element type matches the field's `value_type`: string for `string`, number for `number`, boolean for `boolean`. Empty when the field has no fixed set of values.

scopes.description: RUM scopes this field appears in.

queryable.description: True if this field can be used in DQL/SQL queries.

RumFieldListRequest.description: Filter parameters for listing RUM field definitions.

scopes.description: Filter by RUM data scopes. Valid values: `session`, `view`, `action`, `error`, `resource`, `long_task`, `vital`, `issue`, `sourcemap`.

is_facet.description: When true, return only facet-enabled fields. When false or omitted, return all fields.

is_crash.description: Whether the error caused an app crash.

regression.description: Regression metadata. Present only when a previously resolved issue re-occurred.

regressed_at.description: Timestamp when the regression was detected.

regressed_at_version.description: Application version in which the regression was observed.

resolved_at.description: Timestamp of the previous resolution before the regression.

start_time.description: Start of time range, millisecond timestamp.

end_time.description: End of time range, millisecond timestamp. Maximum range: 183 days.

dql.description: DQL query for advanced filtering. Cannot be used with `sql`.

sql.description: SQL-style query for advanced filtering. Cannot be used with `dql`.

error_required.description: If `true`, only return issues with at least one associated error event.

RumWebhookTestRequest.description: Parameters for sending a sample RUM alert webhook.

webhook_url.description: Webhook URL to receive the sample alert event.

RumWebhookTestResponse.description: Result of the webhook test delivery.

ok.description: Whether the webhook endpoint accepted the sample event.

status_code.description: HTTP status code returned by the webhook endpoint. 0 when the request did not receive a response.

message.description: `ok` on success, otherwise the delivery error message.

SourcemapBinaryImage.description: Loaded binary image from a crash report.

uuid.description: Build UUID identifying the binary or dSYM.

is_system.description: Whether this binary belongs to the operating system.

load_address.description: Runtime address. Accepts a hex string such as `0x100000000` or a decimal integer.

max_address.description: Runtime address. Accepts a hex string such as `0x100000000` or a decimal integer.

arch.description: CPU architecture for this binary image.

SourcemapCodeSnippet.description: One source-code line returned around an enriched frame.

converted.description: Whether the frame was successfully symbolicated or deobfuscated.

third_party.description: Whether the frame is from third-party or system libraries.

key.description: Storage key uniquely identifying this sourcemap file.

git_repository_url.description: Git repository URL associated with this build.

git_commit_sha.description: Git commit SHA for this build.

updated_at.description: Last update timestamp, Unix epoch seconds.

metadata.description: Free-form key-value metadata attached to the sourcemap. Shape depends on the upload client; common keys include `git_repository_url` and `git_commit_sha` (though those are also promoted to top-level fields).

start_time.description: Start of upload time range, Unix epoch milliseconds. Must be > 0 and before `end_time`.

end_time.description: End of upload time range, Unix epoch milliseconds. Maximum window: 365 days.

type.description: Platform type. Defaults to `browser` when omitted.

services.description: Filter by service names. Up to 100 values.

versions.description: Filter by version strings. Up to 100 values.

query.description: Substring match on the minified URL (browser) or build ID (android). Max 200 characters.

build_id.description: Android only. Filter by Gradle plugin build identifier. Max 200 characters.

uuid.description: iOS only. Filter by dSYM bundle UUID. Max 200 characters.

type.description: Source platform. Defaults to `browser` when omitted.

service.description: Application or service name used when the sourcemap was uploaded.

version.description: Application version used when the sourcemap was uploaded.

stack.description: Raw stack trace to parse and enrich.

near.description: Number of nearby meaningful source lines to return around converted frames.

no_cache.description: Skip cached enrich results. Intended for debugging.

build_id.description: Android build ID for Gradle plugin 1.13.0 and later.

variant.description: Android build variant used by older Gradle plugin versions.

arch.description: Android NDK architecture such as `arm`, `arm64`, `x86`, or `x64`.

source_type.description: Android error source type. Use `ndk` with `arch` for native symbolication.

binary_images.description: Loaded binary images from an iOS crash report.

SourcemapStackFrame.description: Parsed stack frame fields shared across platforms.

file.description: Source file, URL, or module path.

column.description: Column number for JavaScript or Flutter frames.

method_name.description: Android Java/Kotlin method name without class prefix.

SuccessEnvelope.description: Success response envelope. On every 2xx response, `request_id` identifies the call (also mirrored in the `Flashcat-Request-Id` header) and `data` holds the endpoint-specific payload. Failure responses use a different shape — see `ErrorResponse`.

request_id.description: Unique ID for this request. Mirrored in the Flashcat-Request-Id response header. Include it when reporting issues.

data.description: Endpoint-specific payload. See each operation's 200 response schema.

RumSessionReplayMetaRequest.description: Look up replay metadata for a single RUM session.

ts.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds of the session start time. Optional; disambiguates when a session ID has been reused across different time windows.

id.description: RUM application ID the session belongs to.

type.description: Device type recorded for the session, e.g. `desktop`, `mobile`, `tablet`.

is_active.description: Whether the session was still active as of the last recorded event.

server_time_delta.description: Clock skew in milliseconds between the client and Flashduty's servers, added to client timestamps for correction.

source.description: SDK platform that recorded the session.

start.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the session started.

end.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the session ended (or was last updated, if still active).

source.description: SDK platform that recorded the view.

view_id.description: Unique ID of the view within the session.

name.description: View name, typically the route or screen name.

url.description: URL (web) or screen identifier (mobile) associated with the view.

loading_type.description: How the view was entered, e.g. `initial_load`, `route_change`.

container_source.description: SDK platform of the container app, when this view is embedded (e.g. a WebView inside a native app).

container_view_id.description: View ID of the containing view, when this view is embedded.

server_time_delta.description: Clock skew in milliseconds between the client and Flashduty's servers, added to client timestamps for correction.

end.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the view ended.

start.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the view started.

is_active.description: Whether the view was still active as of the last recorded event.

RumReplayForegroundPeriod.description: A time span during which the app was in the foreground (mobile sessions).

start.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the foreground period started.

end.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds when the foreground period ended.

view_id.description: View ID active during this foreground period.

RumSessionReplayMetaItem.description: Replay metadata for a session: the application, device, session bounds, and every recorded view.

views.description: Every view recorded during the session, in chronological order.

foreground_periods.description: Foreground periods across the session (mobile sessions only; empty for web).

RumSessionReplaySegmentsRequest.description: Page through the recorded replay segments of a session, or a single view within it.

view_id.description: Restrict results to segments belonging to this view. Omit to page through the entire session.

search_after_ctx.description: Pagination cursor from a previous call. Take it from the `search_after_ctx` field (URL mode) or the `X-Search-After-Ctx` response header (streaming mode).

ts.description: Unix timestamp in milliseconds. When set (and `search_after_ctx` is empty), seeks to the most recent full-snapshot segment at or before this time instead of starting from the beginning.

url_mode.description: When `true`, return presigned download URLs as a JSON envelope instead of streaming segment bytes. Defaults to `false`.

limit.description: Maximum number of segments to return. 1-99, default 20.

RumSessionReplaySegmentsResult.description: Presigned segment URLs, returned only when `url_mode` is `true`.

items.description: Presigned, time-limited URLs (valid 1 hour) for downloading each segment's raw compressed bytes.

search_after_ctx.description: Pagination cursor to pass as `search_after_ctx` on the next call. Empty when this page was the last one.

RumRuleFilter.description: One condition in a RUM rule filter group.

RumRuleFilters.description: Filter groups joined by OR; each group joins its conditions with AND.

RumErrorIngestionRule.description: An error ingestion rule that can discard matching RUM error events.

RumPresetSeverityRule.description: A rule that assigns a severity to matching RUM issues.

severity.description: Severity assigned when the rule matches.

priority.description: Evaluation order; lower values run first.

RumErrorIngestionRuleListRequest.description: Parameters for listing error ingestion rules.

RumErrorIngestionRuleCreateRequest.description: Parameters for creating an error ingestion rule.

RumErrorIngestionRuleUpdateRequest.description: Parameters for updating an error ingestion rule.

RumPresetSeverityRuleListRequest.description: Parameters for listing preset severity rules.

RumPresetSeverityRuleCreateRequest.description: Parameters for creating a preset severity rule.

RumPresetSeverityRuleUpdateRequest.description: Parameters for updating a preset severity rule.

RumRuleActionRequest.description: Parameters for an operation on one rule.

RumPresetSeverityRuleReorderRequest.description: Parameters for moving one preset severity rule before another.

target_rule_id.description: Rule ID that receives the moved rule.

RumRuleHistoryRevertRequest.description: Parameters for restoring a rule-set snapshot.

RumRuleHistoryListRequest.description: Parameters for listing rule-set history snapshots.

limit.description: Snapshot count per page. Defaults to 20 and is capped at 100.

RumErrorIngestionRuleListResponse.description: Error ingestion rules for one application.

RumErrorIngestionRuleCreateResponse.description: Identifier and name of the created error ingestion rule.

RumPresetSeverityRuleListResponse.description: Preset severity rules for one application.

RumPresetSeverityRuleCreateResponse.description: Identifier, name, and priority of the created preset severity rule.

RumErrorIngestionRuleHistoryItem.description: One saved error ingestion rule-set snapshot.

updated_by.description: User ID that created the snapshot.

updated_by_name.description: Name of the user who created the snapshot.

RumPresetSeverityRuleHistoryItem.description: One saved preset severity rule-set snapshot.

updated_by.description: User ID that created the snapshot.

updated_by_name.description: Name of the user who created the snapshot.
